record.paper_title: Stellar model calibrations with the Ai Phe binary system. Open questions about the robustness of the fit
record.original_question: Can binary systems in the approximately 1.2–1.5 M⊙ mass range be used to robustly constrain free parameters in stellar evolution calculations, or are the resulting calibrations too sensitive to uncertain surface-[Fe/H] evolution and related modelling choices? In the specific case of Ai Phe, which of the competing surface-metallicity scenarios is the more reliable description of the system, and can precise measurements of the individual stellar surface [Fe/H] values discriminate between those scenarios?

evidence.quote: As such this investigation raises some doubt as to the robustness of the calibrations obtained in the mass range between 1.2 M⊙ and 1.5 M⊙.
every system provides different challenges and poses interesting questions about the possibility to use them to constrain free parameters in stellar model computations.
In this specific case, precise measurements of individual surface [Fe/H] would be of utmost importance in helping us to judge which scenario is the most reliable.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider detached eclipsing binary stellar systems in which both components have masses in the range 1.2 M⊙ ≲ M ≲ 1.5 M⊙, with very precisely measured masses, radii, and effective temperatures. Stellar evolution codes used to model such systems contain free or weakly constrained parameters (e.g., the convective core overshooting efficiency, the efficiency of microscopic diffusion at the surface, mixing length, initial helium abundance, and initial chemical composition), and standard fitting pipelines determine these parameters together with the system age by matching computed stellar tracks to observations.

(a) Determine whether, in this mass range, binary-system observations of the above quality suffice to yield calibrations of the free model parameters (in particular the core overshooting efficiency) that are robust against the modelling choice for the evolution of the surface iron-to-hydrogen ratio [Fe/H] — specifically, against the choice between (i) a scenario in which microscopic diffusion is allowed to modify the surface [Fe/H] and (ii) a scenario in which competing mixing processes cancel out this surface depletion so that the surface [Fe/H] tracks the initial value.

(b) For the specific detached eclipsing binary Ai Phoenicis (Ai Phe), with its currently available precise mass and radius measurements for the two components, decide which of the two surface-metallicity scenarios (i)–(ii) above gives the more reliable description of the system, and determine whether a precise spectroscopic measurement of the individual surface [Fe/H] values of the two components is sufficient to discriminate between these scenarios.
artifact.status_search_result: The investigation establishes that in the 1.2–1.5 M⊙ range, calibrations (especially of core overshooting) are not robust to the assumed surface-[Fe/H] evolution scenario, and that for Ai Phe an unambiguous fit cannot currently be obtained. The discriminating role of precise individual surface [Fe/H] measurements is highlighted as needed but not yet performed. No follow-up resolving these questions appears in the available literature, so the questions remain open.

status_evidence.title: Stellar model calibrations with the Ai Phe binary system (A&A)
status_evidence.snippet: a sharp calibration of the core overshooting parameter was not achievable; differences between calibrations under the two surface-[Fe/H] scenarios are quite relevant.
status_evidence.claim: Calibration is not robust to surface-[Fe/H] scenario in this mass range; for Ai Phe no unambiguous fit is achieved.

status_evidence.title: Ai Phe binary system - ADS
status_evidence.snippet: Confirms difficulty in achieving sensible calibration of free parameters of stellar models using binary systems even with very accurate masses and radii.
status_evidence.claim: The question of robust calibration in the 1.2–1.5 M⊙ regime remains unresolved.
